x: Barry Ingarfield and Doug Fotheringham, now there's two I can thrash - or can I ? After the One Hour I thought Len Duquemin's age had at last caught up on him but where is he now?right up there again far out of my failing sight.
Doug Fotheringham 45:13 with 8:10 allowance won the Handicap and Barry Ingarfield, a new signing from Ipswich, 45:59 with 8:40 allowance took third.

Barry Ingarfield is the latest addition to the Wimbledon school and his times have also improved steadily through the winter. Our older established walkers also seem determined to make their mark so we enter the National season as confident as we can be that some good results should be coming our way.

Doug Fotheringham was not on top form but finished second proving too strong for a fast improving Barry Ingarfield. Those two distance stalwarts Ray Hall and Pat Duncan did their best to screw each other throughout the race with Pat pulling away up the last hill " out of earshot ".
Barry Ingarfield confirmed his recent form with Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton both supporting well. Newcomer from Ireland John Johnson failed to break 100 minutes but scored in the team.

This gave Barry Ingarfield his chance for gold and how he used it producing a personal best and breaking 82 for the first time! Up front Carl Lawton finished fifth ahead of Wilf Wesch who was just clear of Bob Coates.
Barry Ingarfield and Brian Ward have also come to the fore and Pat Duncan is now busy trying to convince Dave King that he is needed for the longer ones.

Good performances by both Ray Middleton 47 : 17 and Barry Ingarfield 49 : 28 in the Southern Counties 10,000 Metres on May 16th. While on May 2nd, Ray once again triumphed over his fellow postmen to win the 15 Kilos in 72 :25.
Pat Duncan and Brian Ward both walked steady races but Barry Ingarfield was unhappy although he hung on determindly to close in the 8 to retain the Nijmegan Shield.
Barry Ingarfield broke 3 Hours for the first time at Middlesex. In Guernsey the Commonwealth Games Trial was won by John Moullin in 2 : 46 : 00 with Len Duquemin 43 seconds behind.

Over the short ones Barry Ingarfield should also feature after a hard summer. On May 30th the Cambridge section scored a one/two for Belgrave with Bobby Barnes winning the 3,000 Metres in 16.42 18 seconds clear of Barry Wallman.
Good performances from Ray Middleton and Barry Ingarfield could not make up for the absence of some of our other stars so 7th Team place was all we got.
High placings by Carl Lawton 4th 44:54, J.Moullin 46:09 13th and Barry Ingarfield 16th 47:27 enabled Pat Duncan 39th in 50:37 to stage a desperate sprint to snatch second team position.
Carl Lawton turned the tables on Ray Middleton with Barry Ingarfield coming up with a very fast time as well.
In the 5 Mile Yacht at Crystal Palace Ray Middleton finished 3rd in 37:38 Carl Lawton 4th in 37:45 and Barry Ingarfield 7th in 39:09

Personal bests for Barry Ingarfield and Carl Lawton with Ray Middleton taking second place in the Civil Service championship. Second claim John Duckett slipped under the hour for the first time and evergreen Dave McMullen turned in a snappy 57.48 which made some of our younger members blush a bit.

With a superb display of speed Wilf Wesch beat 50 Minutes and Bob Dobson by just 1 second. Barry Ingarfield was disqualified and although McMullen deputised to good effect we were not up to the strength of Basildon in the team.

Recent team performances had been disappointing for our boys but on their own course there was no mistake, Carl Lawton had a steady race but John Moullin and a much improved Barry Ingarfield were well to the fore to give Belgrave victory by 9 points from the Basildon squad.

Barry Ingarfield was expected to take the Horwood Cup without much trouble but he pushed away from the start to win by some three minutes from John Bromley with Manx man John Wilkinson in third place.

Less excusable was Barry Ingarfield who put paid to any chances the team may have had when he too was pulled. Carl Lawton once again excelled with a personal best which put him among the really fast boys and ahead of Commonwealth Bronze Medallist Bill Sutherland.
In the same race Barry Ingarfield recorded a personal best 78:16 with Dave McMullen finishing 6th in 82:58. Joe and Percy Wilson brought up the rear in 104:24 and 105:52 respectively.

John Moullin ducked under 80 and hed[illegible] of Barry Ingarfield by six seconds to take the third place medal. In the Junior the holder, Paul Duckett, was suprised to find the you police cadet Whitehead well ahead.
Some safe walking from Barry Ingarfield and strong backing in the shape of John Bromley Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton gave Belgrave an unexpected 2nd place in this 'Junior' championship.
Barry Ingarfield walked strongly for fourth place with John Moullin closing the team in. A word of praise for Whitehead who, after a personal best for five miles struggled on gamely to finish.

In the Middlesex Championship Barry Ingarfield recorded a sharp 77:43 in 4th Pos while in the Sussex race Pat Duncan was 9th in 85:59 "It's fatal to walk when the Brighton running squad are out" said our man after the race!

Barry Ingarfield and Dave McMullen both walked good races, prepared to shoulder the burden if necessary. Belgrave men were also prominent in the county race with Wilf and Carl featuring in Surrey's 2nd position and Alan Callow scoring for Lancashire who finished 3rd.

Wilf Wesch thrashed his german team mates for an impressive third place while Ray Middleton, Barry Ingarfield and John Moullin made up for the absence of some of our other stars to ensure that Belgrave won the team event.
Barry Ingarfield started fast but faded over the second half while Dave DeBondi celebrated his return to fitness by walking the last 10 miles nearly five minutes faster than his first 10.

Middlesex and the suprise of the day as Barry Ingarfield shot through 5 Miles in 36 Minutes, 10 in 74 for a final time of 2:41:43. It is a pity that one of Barry's finest performances to date should be marred by an obviously short first 10.
Barry Ingarfield we hope can show consistently the form he has produced on occasions and with Len Duquemin back in training and eligible for the Post Office John Moullin may also reappear.
Another winner was Barry Ingarfield in the Enfield 10 Kilos his 48.50 brought him in ahead of veteran Ken Easlea. Ray Middleton should have won but went off course.
The other side of town saw Alan Callow and Barry Ingarfield covering 12,323 Metres and 12,276 metres to finish 13th and 15th respectively in the Highgate 1 Hour Track Walks.
Carl Lawton managed to complete the distance although far short of his best road performance. Bob Coates and Barry Ingarfield also completed the distance.
Barry Ingarfield tried to prove that he was the star of the day and suffered disqualification as a result. Ray Middleton almost had Lawton on the line after powering through the field.

Unfortunately, Barry Ingarfield dropped back to 26th place after making an attempt to win the race in the first 5 miles. Len Duquemin made a valiant attempt but was forced to retire due to a heavy cold.
